title: Caching Repeated Work: Prefix, Prompt and Semantic Caches
summary: The cheapest token is the one you never compute. This lesson covers reusing the KV cache for shared prompt prefixes, the arithmetic of provider prompt-caching discounts and break-even hit rates, designing prompts for cache hits, and semantic caches that answer repeated questions with a similarity threshold and a risk of false hits.
objectives: Explain prefix (KV) caching and compute the prefill time and cost it saves for a shared prompt prefix
Compute the expected cost per request under a provider's cached-read discount and cache-write premium, and the break-even hit rate
Structure prompts so the stable part comes first and estimate hit rate from request rate and cache lifetime
Compute a semantic cache's hit rate and false-hit rate at a similarity threshold and choose the threshold by expected value
Decide what to cache, for how long, and how to keep it correct and private
prerequisites: You should know prefill and the KV cache ([Context Windows, Prefill and the KV Cache](/learn/model-foundations/context-and-kv-cache)), PagedAttention blocks ([Batching and Scheduling](/learn/inference-and-serving/batching)) and cosine similarity of embeddings ([Embeddings](/learn/model-foundations/embeddings)).
